title: Cleaning up space
summary_es: Una ingeniera explica qué es la basura espacial, por qué es peligrosa y cómo piensa su equipo retirar satélites muertos.
prediction_prompt: What do you think "space junk" is, and why might it be a problem?

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: My guest today is Helen Marsh, an engineer who works on removing rubbish from space. Helen, welcome.

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: Thanks, Chris. It's good to be here.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: Let's start with the basics. What exactly is space junk?

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: It's anything in orbit that no longer has a purpose: dead satellites, old rocket parts, even flakes of paint.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: Flakes of paint don't sound very dangerous.

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: You'd be surprised. Up there, objects travel at around seven kilometres a second.

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: At that speed, something the size of a coin can destroy a satellite.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: And how much of this stuff is there?

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: We're tracking about thirty-five thousand objects larger than a tennis ball.

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: But there are probably a million smaller pieces that we simply can't see.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: That's alarming. Is it getting worse?

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: Yes, and quickly. Every collision creates more pieces, which then cause more collisions.

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: If we do nothing, some orbits could become too dangerous to use within a few decades.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: Why should ordinary people care about that?

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: Because modern life depends on satellites: weather forecasts, navigation, even paying by card.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: I hadn't thought about it like that. So what's your team doing about it?

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: We're building a spacecraft that can catch a dead satellite with a robotic arm.

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: Then it pulls the satellite down until it burns up in the atmosphere.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: It sounds like science fiction.

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: It did ten years ago. Our first test mission is planned for the year after next.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: Who pays for all this? It can't be cheap.

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: That's the difficult part. Nobody wants to pay for cleaning up somebody else's mess.

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: I'd compare it to the oceans. Everyone uses them, but nobody feels responsible for them.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: So is the real problem technical or political?

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: Honestly, I'd say political. The technology is nearly ready, but the international rules aren't.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: Are you optimistic?

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: Cautiously. Companies have finally realised that a crowded orbit is bad for business.

segments.speaker: helen
segments.text: Once money is involved, things tend to move faster.

segments.speaker: chris
segments.text: Helen Marsh, thank you very much.

connected_speech.explanation_es: *You'd* = *you would*. La *d* se pega a *be* y casi no se oye.
*at* es débil (/ət/) y se enlaza con *around*.
La *t* de *can't* desaparece delante de *see*: lo negativo se nota en la vocal larga.
*hadn't* pierde la *t* y *thought about it* se dice seguido.

connected_speech.phrase: what's your team doing about it
connected_speech.explanation_es: *what's your* se funde (/ˈwɒtʃə/) y *about it* se enlaza.

connected_speech.phrase: is planned for the year after next
connected_speech.ipa: /ɪz ˈplænd fə ðə ˈjɪər ˈɑːftə ˈnekst/
connected_speech.explanation_es: *for* suena /fə/; *year after* se enlaza con una /r/.
*I'd* = *I would*: sirve para dar una opinión con prudencia.
*tend to* pierde la *d* y *to* es débil.

tasks.prompt: What is the interview mainly about?

The problem of rubbish in orbit and what to do about it
How new satellites are designed and built today

tasks.prompt: How does Helen feel about the future?

options.text: Hopeful, but with some caution
Completely confident about everything
Deeply pessimistic

tasks.rationale_es: A *Are you optimistic?* contesta *Cautiously*: optimista, con cautela.

tasks.prompt: Why can a tiny object be so dangerous in space?

options.text: Because it is extremely hot
Because nobody can see it coming
Because of its enormous speed

tasks.rationale_es: A siete kilómetros por segundo, algo del tamaño de una moneda destruye un satélite.

tasks.prompt: Complete the sentence with a number.
tasks.text: Scientists are tracking about {{1}} objects larger than a tennis ball.
tasks.rationale_es: *Thirty-five thousand*: 35 000. Las piezas pequeñas, que no se ven, serían un millón.

tasks.prompt: Why is the amount of junk growing so fast?

options.text: Because more rockets are launched every single year
Because crashes produce pieces that cause further crashes
Because old satellites are abandoned

tasks.rationale_es: Cada choque crea más fragmentos, que provocan más choques: un círculo vicioso.

tasks.prompt: Helen says some orbits may become unusable within a few decades.
tasks.rationale_es: *Too dangerous to use within a few decades*.

tasks.prompt: Which of these does Helen NOT mention as depending on satellites?

options.text: Weather forecasts
Card payments
Television

tasks.rationale_es: Menciona la previsión del tiempo, la navegación y los pagos con tarjeta. De la televisión no dice nada.

tasks.prompt: How will Helen's spacecraft deal with a dead satellite?

options.text: It will grab it and drag it down to burn
It will push it further out into deep space
It will break it into small pieces

tasks.rationale_es: Lo atrapa con un brazo robótico y lo baja hasta que se desintegra en la atmósfera.

tasks.prompt: The first test mission has already taken place.
tasks.rationale_es: Está prevista *for the year after next*: dentro de dos años.

tasks.prompt: Why does Helen compare space to the oceans?

options.text: Both are extremely large and still mostly unexplored
Both are used by everyone but looked after by no one
Both are difficult to reach

tasks.rationale_es: Todos los usan y nadie se hace responsable: por eso nadie quiere pagar la limpieza.

tasks.prompt: In Helen's opinion, the main obstacle is…

options.text: a lack of agreement between countries
a lack of suitable technology at the moment
a lack of trained engineers

tasks.rationale_es: La tecnología está casi lista; lo que falta son reglas internacionales.

tasks.prompt: Helen believes that business interests will help to solve the problem.
tasks.rationale_es: Las empresas ven que una órbita saturada es mala para el negocio, y con dinero de por medio todo va más rápido.
